title: A local viscosity change can reduce disc density for 13 ASASSN-14ko cycles with little luminosity change in a prescribed thin-disc model
abstract: We test whether steady AGN luminosity excludes a local disc-density change during the ASASSN-14ko timing stall. In a prescribed thin-disc diffusion model, a factor-20 local viscosity increase reduces density at 200 gravitational radii to 0.160 after 1.14 source-frame years. It stays at 0.091-0.160 for the next 13 cycles. Total viscous power is only 1.026-1.042 times its initial value during that interval, and inner mass flux is unchanged to numerical precision. The initial power increase is 14.3 percent. A second, fixed-viscosity gap test gives little luminosity change but needs a 53-solar-mass deficit at a reference luminosity. The main test conserves mass. These results limit the earlier steady-disc exclusion: luminosity constrains stress times density, not density alone when viscosity changes. They do not fit the observed WISE curve or the stellar orbit. The stress change, thermal closure, moving crossings and renewed period decrease remain unexplained. Code, checks, original model outputs and source hashes are supplied.
